items.title: Paid media variables and complexities
items.detail: Scott to send the variables he walked through (product vs. lead gen, locations, app, CRM, special verticals) so the Paid drafts can be corrected.

items.title: Kristina's PR toolkit doc
items.detail: Kristina mentioned a doc she started for the PR toolkit. It isn't in Drive search, so the PR drafts were built without it. Please share it.

items.title: Where the proprietary line sits for PR
items.detail: Kristina worried a PR toolkit gives away too much. Drafts stick to client readiness (bios, spokesperson, media kit) and leave out media lists, Muck Rack and the HARO agent. Confirm that's the right line.

items.title: Confirm the SEO toolkit owner
items.detail: The RevOps files list the SEO toolkit owner as not yet named. The drafts assume Shema Al-Darwish.

items.title: Who reviews the tracking steps?
items.detail: Tracking now lives inside RevOps (Toolkit 7: Can You See What Your Marketing Does?, owned by Dallas) and Paid (Toolkit 3: Which Conversions Should You Track?, owned by Scott), with Search Console and Bing in SEO. Scott suggested Alex or someone strong in Tag Manager review the setup steps.

items.title: Automated check-in after someone uses a toolkit
items.detail: Dallas wants a 'how did it go?' follow-up from the toolkit owner after a visitor gets their plan. The site has no backend, so this needs an opt-in form (ecosystem form, HubSpot or Mailchimp) on each results panel plus a short email series.

items.title: Minimum budget and default split
items.detail: Paid drafts treat $1,000/mo as ready for one campaign and $1,500 to add a second, with 70–85% on the main campaign. Confirm or correct.

items.title: Google-only in v1, or add Meta and Microsoft Ads?
items.detail: Drafts cover Google Ads only. Also: should Standard Shopping beat Performance Max under $1,500/mo, and should brand Search be the default second campaign?

items.title: Conversion defaults
items.detail: Import GA4 key events or use Google Ads tags in Tag Manager? Which CRM stages (MQL, SQL, closed-won) go back to Google Ads by default, and is ~30 conversions in 30 days the bar before target CPA/ROAS?

items.title: Click through every menu path once
items.detail: The RevOps 7 and Paid steps name exact menus in GA4, Tag Manager, Google Ads, Meta, LinkedIn, Shopify, Mailchimp, Klaviyo and more. They were written from current knowledge and need one check by a practitioner before launch.

items.title: AI search position and checks
items.detail: Is “allow search bots; blocking AI training bots is the client's choice” Big Leap's official position? Which AI-search checks stay (OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, Bing for Copilot/ChatGPT), and should llms.txt be added?

items.title: A third SEO toolkit?
items.detail: Should there be a content and keyword starter toolkit, or does that stay expert-only? Same question for AI visibility tracking setup and redesign redirect checks.

items.title: Response bar and formats
items.detail: Is 24–48 hours the right reply bar for journalists, or the ~5-business-day interview commitment used before? Are 50/150-word bios and the headshot spec (2000px+, 4:5, 16:9, 1:1) what the team actually asks for?

items.title: Paid podcast-guest lists
items.detail: Do paid podcast-guest lists belong in a v2 as a 90-day jumpstart, or only as a “talk to Kristina” item? Is it OK to mention reporter-request services as a generic category?

items.title: Which email platforms to support first
items.detail: Drafts cover Mailchimp, Klaviyo, HubSpot and Constant Contact. Drop any, or add Brevo or ActiveCampaign? Should Mailchimp lead the examples, since Big Leap moved its own email to Mailchimp?

items.title: Email benchmarks and the dollar estimate
items.detail: Are the scorecard ranges in Email 3 the ones Erica uses (for example spam complaints under 0.1%, never over 0.3%)? Should Email 2 keep its rule-of-thumb estimate of what missing flows leave on the table?

items.title: Email scope: legal table, sign-up forms, SMS
items.detail: Should legal review the email-law table in Email 1? Is a 4th toolkit on sign-up forms and lead magnets wanted? Does SMS stay under “Where it gets complex”?

items.title: Test on real Safari, Firefox and phones
items.detail: Every page was tested in Chromium at 320–1920px, light and dark, with no overflow or errors, and the code avoids Safari-unsafe features. Firefox, Safari and Samsung Internet weren't available here, so give it one pass on an iPhone and a Mac before launch.

items.title: Usage tracking on the toolkit site
items.detail: No analytics on the site yet. Add a GA4 property, or the ecosystem tracking, to see which toolkits get used and finished.

items.title: Swap 'Talk to …' buttons for real scheduler links
items.detail: Every “Talk to Dallas / Scott / Shema / Kristina / Erica” button points to bigleap.com/contact-us (UTM-tagged) for now. Each owner should send a meeting scheduler link.

items.title: Content Go/No-Go toolkit
items.detail: Email Marketing is now its own series (Erica Pounder, 3 draft toolkits). Content is the one service still without a toolkit; the RevOps pages keep a hidden cross-link slot for Whitney Sorensen's Content Go/No-Go toolkit.

items.title: Public link vs. private drafts
items.detail: GitHub Pages on this account is public: anyone with the link can open the drafts. They carry a Draft banner and are hidden from search engines. Going private needs GitHub Enterprise or a host with access control, such as Cloudflare Access.

items.title: Custom address
items.detail: The site lives at bigl3ap.github.io/bigleap-diy-toolkits. A subdomain like tools.bigleap.com can point here with one DNS record if wanted.

items.title: Where the toolkits live on bigleap.com
items.detail: Coby expects them to become front and center over time, and to feed the 90-day foundational model James is building. Placement and priority on the site are still undecided.

items.title: Line up with Coby's gap audit
items.detail: Each new toolkit opens with a 'what's already in place?' check, based on Coby's gap audit. Confirm the shared Business Profile fields match what the audit and sales team need.

items.title: “Small Leaps” as the program name
items.detail: The site now frames the toolkits as Small Leaps: clients make small leaps on their own with the free toolkits, then make the Big Leap when they hire us. Confirm the name for public use (hero copy, journey map, website mockups) and whether marketing wants it in the nav.

items.title: Agency Brands routing for toolkit leads
items.detail: The journey map assumes multi-location and larger budgets go to Big Leap, and single-location, smaller-budget local leads can go to LeadGenix. Agree the routing rule and who owns it in HubSpot.

items.title: HubSpot properties and MQL rule for toolkit leads
items.detail: Create contact properties for toolkit used, Business Profile answers and plan gaps, and set the scoring rule the journey map uses: profile fit plus two or more toolkits finished = MQL. Depends on the “email me my plan” opt-in.

items.title: Where tracking sits in the RevOps path
items.detail: Tracking moved out of its own series. The stack check is now RevOps Toolkit 7 (added at the end so the live 1–6 keep their numbers), and conversions are Paid Toolkit 3. Install order suggests tracking could come first in RevOps; say if you want it renumbered.

items.title: Special verticals in Paid
items.detail: Car dealerships and regulated categories (legal, healthcare, finance, housing) get 'talk to Scott' instead of a DIY plan. Confirm the list.

items.title: Confirm RevOps Toolkit 5 is the v2 build
items.detail: Its build doc is labelled v2, but the HTML in Drive was saved before the doc. Check the hosted file is the version you want.

items.title: Toolkit review on next Monday's agenda, invite Alex
items.detail: Coby is taking over the agenda from Carolyn. Next week's call walks through the first drafts.

items.title: Masterclass emails: every track to 7 emails
items.detail: Coby to check with Whitney on the remaining Masterclass emails.

items.title: Ecosystem form on the Masterclass site
items.detail: Dallas and Phil to replace the HubSpot form on the Masterclass site with the new ecosystem form.

items.title: Reporting gap Oct 1–5 vs. client hub start Oct 12
items.detail: Scott flagged a drop-off around Oct 1–5. Dallas confirmed only email marketing moved to Mailchimp, and offered to dig in with Kevin.

items.title: Confirm the “Notice Different / Align to Genuine” definitions
items.detail: The journey map reads them as: Notice Different = the moment a prospect sees we're not another agency pitch; Align to Genuine = help that fits their real situation (honest limits, named experts, proof from their segment); Convert = trigger + offer → booked call. Confirm or correct the wording, and the four segment stories.

items.title: Add the Tag Manager container ID and HubSpot Hub ID
items.detail: Engagement events (diy_*) already go into the dataLayer on every page and widget. Put GTM_ID and HUBSPOT_ID in tools/site_header.py and rerun to send them to GA4 and HubSpot, then add the GA4 event tag on diy_* and mark diy_cta_click and diy_plan_copy as key events.

items.title: Save the HubSpot report for toolkit-sourced pipeline
items.detail: Contacts and deals with original source campaign diy-toolkits, by lifecycle stage, utm_campaign (toolkit) and brand. Counts toward the $400K new marketing-sourced MRR goal.

items.title: Build the plan-delivery and owner check-in email sequence
items.detail: Day 0 plan, Day 3 owner check-in, Day 7 next small leap, Day 14 segment case study, Day 21 plan review. Exits on meeting booked. Needs the “Email me my plan” opt-in form connected first.

items.title: High-intent sales alert workflow
items.detail: HubSpot workflow + Slack post when a prospect hits a launch blocker, finishes 3+ toolkits in 14 days, or revisits Paid 4, RevOps 6 or Email 3.

items.title: Retargeting audiences for toolkit visitors
items.detail: Started-not-finished and finished-not-booked audiences in Google Ads and Meta; exclude customers and open deals.

items.title: Confirm the example KPI targets
items.detail: Example targets on the journey page (e.g. 3–5% talk-to clicks, 15%+ plans taken) are starting points. Set real targets after 60 days of baseline data.

items.title: Unify the Business Profile box across all toolkits (Draft 2)
items.detail: RevOps 1–6 have no “Answer 8 questions once” box; Paid/PR and SEO/Email show it in two different layouts. Use one shared component everywhere.

items.title: Put “Where it gets complex” in one place on every toolkit (Draft 2)
items.detail: RevOps 1–6 and PR tuck it inside the dark closing panel (“Where the DIY version stops”); Paid, SEO, Email and RevOps 7 show a standalone card before it. Pick one pattern and one name.
